title: introduce-workload-echo-prober-and-granular-kernel-snapshot-reporter
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Adds a microburst-focused workload runner (echo-prober) and a kernel-level snapshot reporter that exports symbolicated samples into the reporting pipeline. No user-facing API changes.
commits: initial: add echo-prober runner scaffold and config flags
reporter: implement kernel snapshot capture and symbolication hooks
integration: wire reporter to pipeline exporter and add unit tests
docs: add README and CLI examples for new runner
fix: address race in sample buffer flush during shutdown
description:
Context and motivation: We need a focused microburst workload that reliably triggers short, high-concurrency token bursts to exercise scheduling and per-kernel tail behaviors observed in customer traces. This PR adds 'echo-prober', a compact runner that issues short, repeated primers and randomized echo sequences to reproduce microburst hotspots, and a new 'kernel_snapshot' reporter that captures lightweight per-kernel samples (stack traces + perf counters) and symbolicates them before exporting to the existing reporting pipeline.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a deterministic microburst workload runner, sampling buffer with edge-aware flush semantics, symbolization hooks that integrate with the symbol cache, an NDJSON exporter adapter for the reporting pipeline, and documentation + CI config to run the new suite in the benchmark lab integration job. The runner emphasizes low-noise collection (short-lived primers, coordinated warmup) so we can isolate kernel-level hotspots without long-run noise.

Checklist: [x] runner implementation and CLI flags for concurrency/epoch length/primer, [x] sampling buffer and flush-on-idle/rate-limit, [x] symbolization integration with symbol-cache service, [x] exporter adapter to pipeline (ndjson), [x] unit tests for buffer and symbolizer, [x] docs and example workload config, [x] CI integration for nightly baseline.

Commits summary: See commit messages above. Notable changes include addition of sample_buffer.go that implements a ring buffer with lock-free snapshots and a bounded background flusher, and reporter.go that collects kernel sample events and batches them into ndjson records with metadata (runner id, epoch, wall time). The symbolizer_test adds a small synthetic vmlinux symbol table to validate symbolication under high submit rates.

Files changed (high level): bench/runners/echo_prober/* — runner and config; bench/reporters/kernel_snapshot/* — main capture and exporter adapter; bench/pipeline/exporters/ndjson_exporter.go — small helper to normalize records; bench/utils/* — new sample buffer and tests; docs/benchmark-lab/echo-prober.md — how-to and analysis notes; scripts/ci/benchmark-lab-integration.yaml — adds nightly job tie-in.

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for buffer and reporter added and passing. Integration CI initially failed on the benchmark-lab-integration job due to an intermittent timeout when symbolizer fetched an external symbol-cache in the sandbox; resolved by adding a short local symbol cache fallback and making symbol fetches optional in test mode. Final CI run shows all checks passing: unit, linters, race-detector, and benchmark-lab-integration (nightly scheduling enabled).

Review conversation (summary):
- Daniel Cortez: Asked for clarification on the buffer flush invariants and whether the flusher could starve under sustained bursts; requested an additional test for concurrent flush + shutdown.
- Author reply: Added sample_buffer_test to explicitly exercise concurrent flush and graceful shutdown; documented invariants in code comments.
- Priya Menon: Questioned symbolization cost and requested an opt-out flag when running long baselines to avoid OTT IO pressure.
- Author reply: Added config flag 'symbolize=false' for long runs and an adaptive backoff for symbol fetches; documented behavior in echo-prober.md.
- Luca Romano: Suggested improving the NDJSON exporter schema to include runner metadata and epoch tagging; also requested a small change to exporter error handling to avoid halting pipeline on single failed record.
- Author reply: Updated exporter_adapter to include runner_id and epoch fields and to log and continue on record-level failures.
- Final: Approvals from Daniel and Priya after the above changes; Luca approved after minor nits.

CI summary: First run: unit tests + lint passed, integration timed out on external symbol fetch. Second run: added local symbol cache fallback and re-ran; all checks passed. CI artifacts include a nightly baseline artifact produced by the new runner (ndjson) which will seed the profiling dashboard.

Performance notes and follow-ups: Initial runs show the echo-prober creates concentrated p99 spikes on kernel scheduling paths; exported kernel snapshots have been consumed by the perf team for a follow-up micro-optimization ticket (ENG-2213). We plan to add a lightweight aggregation view in the reporting pipeline to surface most-common kernel frames within 72 hours of nightly runs.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals. No breaking changes.

Related tickets: ENG-2189 (microburst benchmark suite), ENG-2213 (kernel scheduling follow-up).
review_comments: Daniel Cortez: The lock-free ring buffer looks promising but can you add a unit test that races flush + shutdown? Concern is buffer can be dropped mid-snapshot.
Marisol Vega: Added sample_buffer_test with concurrent flush/shutdown; documented behavior in buffer comments.
Priya Menon: How expensive is symbolization? For long nightly runs we shouldn't hammer symbol-cache - please add opt-out.
Marisol Vega: Added 'symbolize' runtime flag and adaptive backoff; tests cover both modes.
Luca Romano: NDJSON schema should include runner_id and epoch and exporter should not fail the whole pipeline on one bad record.
Marisol Vega: Updated exporter_adapter to include metadata and continue-on-error; added tests for record-level failures.
